    Supported input item types are `message` / `function_call` / `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call` / `custom_tool_call_output` / `reasoning` / `web_search_call`; other types are ignored. Message roles can be `user` / `assistant` / `system` / `developer` (`developer` is treated as `user`). With the `deepseek-flash` model, `input_image` content parts are supported in `user` / `developer` message items and in the `output` of `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output` items; images in `system` or `assistant` messages return a `400` error. If not set, the model's default thinking behavior is used (enabled by default). For compatibility with existing software, `minimal` is accepted and mapped to `low`, and `medium` / `xhigh` are accepted and mapped to `high`.

        - `type`: `string`

        - `enum`: `["none","low","high","max"]`

    A list of tools the model may call. Function names must be non-empty, at most 128 characters, match `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`, and be unique across all tools. `function` tools are supported; `web_search` is supported with `deepseek-v4-pro`; other built-in tool types are ignored. Please refer to the [Responses API Guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/responses_api.md) for details.

    ```json
    null
    ```

  - **`tool_choice`** (optional)

    Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model.

    `none` means the model will not call any tool and instead generates a message.

    `auto` (default) means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or more tools.

    `required` means the model must call one or more tools.

    - `maximum`: `20`

    - `nullable`: `true`

    - `default`: `null`

    **Example**

    ```json
    null
    ```

  - **`user`** (optional)

    A custom end-user identifier. We recommend using only ASCII letters, digits, underscores (`_`), and hyphens (`-`). The UTF-8 encoded value must not exceed 512 bytes. Do not include user privacy information.

    - It can be used to distinguish user identities on your side to help us with content safety review, for KVCache isolation, and for scheduling isolation. For more details, please refer to [Rate Limit & Isolation](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/rate_limit.md)

A model response in the OpenAI Responses API format.

### schema-response-input-item

**ResponseInputItem** — `#/components/schemas/ResponseInputItem`

An input item. Supported types are `message` / `function_call` / `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call` / `custom_tool_call_output` / `reasoning` / `web_search_call`; other types are ignored. `reasoning` and `function_call` items are automatically merged into the adjacent assistant message by the server. A `web_search_call` item returned by a previous response can be passed back to restore its search results into the context. Please refer to the [Responses API Guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/responses_api.md#multi-turn-conversation) for the pass-back rules in multi-turn conversations.

- `type`: `object`

- **Properties**

  - **`type`** (optional)

    The type of the input item. For `message` items, this field can be omitted if `role` is present. `custom_tool_call` / `custom_tool_call_output` items are used together with the `apply_patch` custom tool. `web_search_call` items restore the search results of a previous server-side search.

    - `type`: `string`

    - `enum`: `["message","function_call","function_call_output","custom_tool_call","custom_tool_call_output","reasoning","web_search_call"]`

  - **`role`** (optional)

    For `message` items. The role of the message author. `developer` is treated as `user`.

    - `type`: `string`

    - `enum`: `["user","assistant","system","developer"]`

  - **`content`** (optional)

    For `message` items, the message content, either a plain string or a list of `input_text` / `output_text` / `input_image` content parts. For `reasoning` items, a list of `reasoning_text` content parts.

    - **oneOf**

      - oneOf 1

        - title: `Text content`

        - `type`: `string`

      - oneOf 2

        - title: `Array of content parts`

        - `type`: `array`

        - **Array items**

          - Reference: [ResponseInputContentPart](#schema-response-input-content-part) (`#/components/schemas/ResponseInputContentPart`)

  - **`call_id`** (optional)

    For `function_call` / `function_call_output` items. The ID pairing a function call with its output. Must be non-empty and unique, and every `function_call` must have a matching `function_call_output`.

    - `type`: `string`

  - **`name`** (optional)

    For `function_call` items. The name of the function to call.

    - `type`: `string`

  - **`arguments`** (optional)

    For `function_call` items. The arguments to call the function with, in JSON format.

    - `type`: `string`

  - **`output`** (optional)

    For `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output` items. The output of the tool call, either a plain string or a list of `input_text` / `input_image` content parts.

    - **oneOf**

      - oneOf 1

        - title: `Text output`

        - `type`: `string`

        - title: `Array of content parts`

        - `type`: `array`

### schema-response-tool

**ResponseTool** — `#/components/schemas/ResponseTool`

A tool the model may call. `function` defines a function tool — note that in the Responses API format, `name` / `parameters` and other function fields are at the top level of the tool object. `custom` defines a custom tool; only `{"type": "custom", "name": "apply_patch"}` is supported, and other names return a `400` error. `web_search` enables server-side web search and is supported with `deepseek-v4-pro`.

- `type`: `object`

- `required`: `["type"]`

- **Properties**

  - **`type`** (required)

    The type of the tool: `function`, `custom` (only `apply_patch`), or `web_search` (`deepseek-v4-pro` only).

    - `type`: `string`

    - `enum`: `["function","custom","web_search"]`

  - **`name`** (optional)

    For `function` and `custom` tools. The name of the tool. For function tools, must be non-empty, at most 128 characters, match `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`, and be unique across all tools. For custom tools, must be `apply_patch`.

    - `type`: `string`

  - **`description`** (optional)

    For `function` tools. A description of what the function does, used by the model to choose when and how to call the function.

    - `type`: `string`

  - **`parameters`** (optional)

    - Reference: [FunctionParameters](#schema-function-parameters) (`#/components/schemas/FunctionParameters`)

### schema-response-output-item

**ResponseOutputItem** — `#/components/schemas/ResponseOutputItem`

An output item generated by the model. `message` items carry the assistant text, `reasoning` items carry the chain-of-thought, `function_call` items represent function calls, `custom_tool_call` items represent custom tool calls (such as `apply_patch`), `web_search_call` items represent server-side web searches (`deepseek-v4-pro` only), and `tool_search_call` items represent tool searches.

- `type`: `object`

- **Properties**

  - **`type`** (optional)

    The type of the output item: `message` / `reasoning` / `function_call` / `custom_tool_call` / `web_search_call` / `tool_search_call`.

    - `type`: `string`

    - `enum`: `["message","reasoning","function_call","custom_tool_call","web_search_call","tool_search_call"]`

  - **`id`** (optional)

    The unique ID of the output item.

    - `type`: `string`

  - **`status`** (optional)

    The status of the output item.

    - `type`: `string`

    - `enum`: `["in_progress","completed","incomplete"]`

  - **`role`** (optional)

    For `message` items. Always `assistant`.

    - `type`: `string`

    - `enum`: `["assistant"]`

  - **`content`** (optional)

    For `message` items, a list of `output_text` content parts. For `reasoning` items, a list of `reasoning_text` content parts carrying the chain-of-thought in plain text.

    - `type`: `array`

    - **Array items**

      - `type`: `object`

      - **Properties**

        - **`type`** (optional)

          - `type`: `string`

          - `enum`: `["output_text","reasoning_text"]`

        - **`text`** (optional)

          - `type`: `string`

  - **`call_id`** (optional)

    For `function_call` / `custom_tool_call` / `tool_search_call` items. An identifier used when passing the tool output back to the API.

    - `type`: `string`

  - **`name`** (optional)

    For `function_call` / `custom_tool_call` items. The name of the function or custom tool to call.

    - `type`: `string`

  - **`arguments`** (optional)

    For `function_call` items. The arguments to call the function with, as generated by the model in JSON format. Note that the model does not always generate valid JSON, and may hallucinate parameters not defined by your function schema. Validate the arguments in your code before calling your function.

    - `type`: `string`

### schema-response-usage

**ResponseUsage** — `#/components/schemas/ResponseUsage`

Token and server-tool usage statistics for the response. Null in initial streaming events; read usage from the final response.

- `type`: `object`

- `nullable`: `true`

- `required`: `["input_tokens","output_tokens","total_tokens"]`

- **Properties**

  - **`input_tokens`** (required)

    Number of input tokens.

    - `type`: `integer`

  - **`input_tokens_details`** (optional)

    Breakdown of the input tokens.

    - `type`: `object`

    - **Properties**

      - **`cached_tokens`** (optional)

        Number of input tokens that hit the context cache. See [Context Caching](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/kv_cache.md).

        - `type`: `integer`

  - **`output_tokens`** (required)

    Number of output tokens.

    - `type`: `integer`

  - **`output_tokens_details`** (optional)

    Breakdown of the output tokens.

    - `type`: `object`

    - **Properties**

      - **`reasoning_tokens`** (optional)

        Number of reasoning (chain-of-thought) tokens generated by the model.

        - `type`: `integer`

  - **`total_tokens`** (required)

    Total number of tokens used in the request (input + output).

    - `type`: `integer`

  - **`server_tool_use`** (optional)

    - title: `Server tool usage`

    Successful server-side web search and page-fetch counts, separate from token usage. Present only when tool\_search or tool\_fetch is greater than zero; otherwise omitted. Both fields are present when this object is returned. In streaming responses, read response.usage from the terminal response.completed, response.incomplete, or response.failed event. These are cumulative counts, not deltas. See [Server tool usage](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/responses_api.md#server-tool-usage).

    - `type`: `object`

    - `required`: `["tool_search","tool_fetch"]`

    - **Properties**

      - **`tool_search`** (required)

        Number of successful web search queries. A search with multiple queries can add more than one; failed queries and queries with no results are not counted. This field can be used as a basis for billing.

        - `type`: `integer`

        - `minimum`: `0`

      - **`tool_fetch`** (required)

        Number of successful page fetches performed by open\_page or find\_in\_page. Failed attempts are not counted. This field can be used as a basis for billing.

        - `type`: `integer`

        - `minimum`: `0`

    **Example**

    ```json
    {
      "tool_search": 1,
      "tool_fetch": 0
    }
    ```

### schema-response-input-image-content-part

**ResponseInputImageContentPart** — `#/components/schemas/ResponseInputImageContentPart`

- title: `Image content part`

An image content part. Processed as a real image. Allowed only in `user` / `developer` message items and in the `output` of `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output` items; images in `system` or `assistant` messages return a `400` error ("Image in system message is unsupported" / "Image in assistant message is unsupported").

- `type`: `object`

- `required`: `["type"]`

- **Properties**

  - **`type`** (required)

    The type of the content part, in this case `input_image`.

    - `type`: `string`

    - `enum`: `["input_image"]`

  - **`image_url`** (optional)

    The image source, either an `http(s)` URL of the image (max 8192 characters) or a base64-encoded data URL (`data:image/jpeg;base64,...`). Supported formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP. Mutually exclusive with `file_id`: passing neither returns a `400` error ("input\_image must have image\_url or file\_id"); passing both returns a `400` error ("input\_image cannot have both image\_url and file\_id").

    - `type`: `string`

  - **`detail`** (optional)

    Controls how the image is processed. `low` downsamples the image to 512x512 (faster, cheaper). `high`, `original`, and `auto` keep the original image. Ignored when `file_id` is set.

    - `type`: `string`

    - `enum`: `["low","high","original","auto"]`

  - **`file_id`** (optional)

    The ID of an image file uploaded via the [Files API](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/files_api.md), of the form `file-api-...`. Mutually exclusive with `image_url`; `detail` is ignored when `file_id` is set.

    - `type`: `string`

## Search & Fetch Pricing

Search and Fetch are standalone APIs billed per request.

| API    | Unit                          | Price |
| ------ | ----------------------------- | ----- |
| Search | Per 1,000 successful requests | $0.75 |
| Fetch  | Per 1,000 successful requests | $0.75 |

See the [Search & Fetch guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/search.md) for API usage and complete billing rules.

***

## Deduction Rules

For model usage, the expense = number of tokens × price. Search and Fetch are charged per successful request at the rates above.
The corresponding fees will be directly deducted from your topped-up balance or granted balance, with a preference for using the granted balance first when both balances are available.

Product prices may vary and DeepSeek reserves the right to adjust them. We recommend topping up based on your actual usage and regularly checking this page for the most recent pricing information.

# GPT-6.2 Sol > For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to the page URL. > Our go-to model for everyday work, from coding to powering agents at scale. Model ID: `gpt-6.2-sol` GPT-6.2 Sol accepts text and image inputs and produces text. Use it with the Responses API to call tools such as web search and computer use, or to delegate work to subagents with the [Multi-agent beta](/api/docs/guides/responses-multi-agent). The API rejects requests that set reasoning effort to `none`. The Responses API supports [discounted background completion windows](/api/docs/guides/background#use-discounted-completion-windows) in public beta. ## Model details - Input modalities: text, image - Output modalities: text - Unsupported modalities: audio, video - 1,050,000 context window - Maximum input tokens: 922,000 - 128,000 max output tokens - Jun 01, 2026 knowledge cutoff - Reasoning token support ## Pricing Prices are per 1M tokens. See the [pricing page](/api/docs/pricing) for processing tiers and billing details. ### Text tokens | Metric | Price | Unit | | --- | ---: | --- | | Input | $2 | 1M tokens | | Cached input | $0.1 | 1M tokens | | Cache writes | $2.5 | 1M tokens | | Output | $10 | 1M tokens | - The cache write price is for 30 minutes of retention. A 12-hour cache write costs $5 per million tokens for short-context requests at Standard pricing. - For requests with more than 272K input tokens, input and cache rates double and output costs 1.5 times the short-context rate for the full request. - Batch costs 50% of Standard rates.
